verdict.rationale: Restate's flow control lets you set concurrency limits per scope and explicitly claims to 'keep scheduling fair'. That is a first-party way to stop one scope (for example, a tenant) from monopolizing execution, rather than relying on unbounded FIFO. Missing for 10: any documented per-run priority assignment, explicit per-tenant fair-queuing semantics (how a scope maps to a tenant and how fairness is enforced), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I assign priorities to runs and get fair scheduling across tenants instead of a single FIFO queue

citations.quote: Shape traffic with concurrency limits per scope to control cost, protect downstream services, and keep scheduling fair.
Flow control lets you shape the traffic flowing through Restate instead of letting invocations run unbounded.
Shape and limit concurrent invocations with scope
